source.quote: Specification reference: ASTM CS78 Type XI Type I Type VIII Type II Type IX | Compressive 10% Deformation psi 01621 5-9 10-14 13-18 15-21 25-33 | Shear Modulus psi ----- 190-230 280-320 370-410 460-500 600-640 | Modulus of Elasticity psi ----- 110-150 180-220 250-310 320-360 460-500

records.notes: CAUTION. (1) Maker not identified in the file; a near-identical table (1.0-2.0 pcf, same G and E rows) is on builditsolar.com attributed to Foam Products Corp, which I did not open at the source. (2) Text layer is OCR ('ASTM CS78'). (3) G (210 psi) exceeds E (130 psi), not consistent for an isotropic solid with positive Poisson ratio; the shear figure is probably a different test. (4) The Virginia Tech study (record eps-1pcf-virginia-tech) measured E about 967 psi on 1 pcf EPS against a manufacturer figure of about 200 psi, so datasheet E and G read low by a factor of about 5 against measurement. Order of magnitude only. Midpoints are my arithmetic on printed ranges.

gaps: Honeycomb scaling with density: Hexcel's 'HexWeb Honeycomb Attributes and Properties' (2019 file, copyright 2016) gives typical L/W shear strength and modulus versus density only as plotted figures; I did not read values off them and found no printed law. The tables give the data points themselves (HRH-10 stabilized modulus 6 ksi at 1.5 pcf to 90 ksi at 9 pcf).
Aramid honeycomb below 23-24 kg/m3: none found. Lightest listings are Hexcel A1-23-19 (23 kg/m3) and 24 kg/m3 for HRH-10, PN2 and ECA/ECA-I. Plascore PN1 was not opened.

Aluminium honeycomb below 1.0 pcf (16 kg/m3): none found in Hexcel CR III or Plascore PAMG-XR1 ('Densities: 1.0 pcf - 12.0 pcf'). Hexcel Flex-Core lowest is 2.1 pcf. Hexcel ACG-1 / commercial-grade sheet: not located (guessed Hexcel URLs answered with redirects that I did not follow). Plascore PAMG-XR1 gives no stabilized modulus, stabilized strength or crush strength.
Hexcel CR III stabilized-modulus MINIMUM is not printed (typ only).
Plascore PN1 / PK2 / PCGA-XR1 not opened. Euro-Composites ECA-I prints a 'Compression Modulus' without saying bare or stabilised.

EPS EN 13163 declared-property tables (e.g. EPS 30 compressive stress CS(10), E-modulus): not obtained. CEN TS 14933 (Utah-hosted copy) downloaded; its Annex E.2 defines E perpendicular to the faces but I extracted no values.
NCHRP Report 529 (2004) EPS12 initial tangent modulus table: not read (the NAP pages I could open carried no table). Horvath's own E-density relation: not found as a printed equation.

Ossa and Romo, Athanasopoulos et al. 1999 (a DOI 10.1680/gein.6.0149 appeared only in search-engine output), Duskov 1997, Elragi et al.: not opened; their DOIs were left out because I did not fetch or Crossref-check them.

Measured EPS compressive modulus at <= 12 kg/m3 from a paper with tabulated values: not found. The Missirlis fit (10 to 35 kg/m3) is the only measured density series; per-sample points sit in a plot I did not digitise. The Qassim University review (jecs.qu.edu.sa) could not be fetched (connection refused), so its 12 kg/m3 values were not verified.

Measured shear modulus for EPS at <= 12 kg/m3: none. The Vejelis fit starts at EPS50 (density not printed). The 'Type XI' sheet shear value (190-230 psi) is a datasheet range with G greater than E and is flagged unreliable.

Solimide (Evonik/Inspec/Boyd) polyimide foam datasheet with modulus, shear modulus or strength: not found. Boyd's technical paper gives only density 6-8 kg/m3 (5.4-8.8 in another line) and fire data. Only PolyuMAC polyimide foam (NASA study) modulus found, with no shear modulus or strength.

Melamine foam: no datasheet or measured static compression or shear modulus for Basotect other than the indirect 303 kPa Biot fit. The '>9 kPa' strength is a datasheet minimum at 40 % compression, not a yield strength. BASF's own copy of the TI sheet was not opened; the Devtec reseller copy was.
Polyurethane and polyethylene foams near 10 kg/m3: no datasheet with modulus found. BASF Elastopor H ('8 - 16' kg/m3 per a search snippet) not verified; the BASF page returned 404.

Honeycomb values are for 0.5 in (aramid) or 0.625 in (aluminium) test thickness; Hexcel's guide says 'Thicker cores will have a lower usable shear strength than thinner ones'. No thickness correction applied.
